questions.question: Put these stages in the correct order for creating an electromagnet
items: Connect the wire to a battery
Wrap the wire around an iron core
questions.explanation: First, wrap the wire around an iron core, then connect the wire to a battery, increase the current, and finally observe the magnetic effect.

questions.question: Sort each item into the correct category
questions.explanation: More current, more wire turns, and an iron core increase field strength. Relays, circuit breakers, and bells are equipment that use electromagnets.

questions.question: Mark each statement True or False
statements: The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire can be found using the right-hand grip rule.
A solenoid has a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet.
The strength of the magnetic field in a solenoid can be increased by using an iron core.
Increasing the current through a solenoid decreases its magnetic field.
questions.explanation: The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire can be found using the right-hand grip rule (True). A solenoid has a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet (True). The strength of the magnetic field in a solenoid can be increased by using an iron core (True). Increasing the current through a solenoid increases its magnetic field, not decreases (False).
questions.topic_label: Chapter 25: The magnetic effect of current

source.area: Chapter 25: The magnetic effect of current

questions.question: Select ALL that apply
options: Increasing the number of turns in a solenoid increases its magnetic field.
Using an iron core in a solenoid increases its magnetic field.
Removing the iron core from a solenoid decreases its magnetic field.
Using a higher voltage in a solenoid increases its magnetic field.
questions.explanation: Increasing the number of turns in a solenoid increases its magnetic field (True). Using an iron core in a solenoid increases its magnetic field (True). Removing the iron core from a solenoid decreases its magnetic field (True). Using a higher voltage does not necessarily increase the magnetic field, as it depends on the current, which is affected by the resistance of the circuit (False).

questions.question: Mark each statement True or False: The magnetic field strength increases with the current, the number of turns of wire, and the presence of an iron core.
statements: The magnetic field strength increases with the current.
The magnetic field strength decreases with the number of turns of wire.
The presence of an iron core does not affect the magnetic field strength.
The magnetic field strength increases with the presence of an iron core.
questions.explanation: The magnetic field strength of a solenoid increases when you increase the current, increase the number of turns of wire, or add an iron core. All three factors strengthen the field.
marking_criteria: Mark the single statement True (all three factors do increase field strength)

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: Which of the following are applications of electromagnets?
questions.explanation: Relays, circuit breakers, and bells all use electromagnets to function. Electric motors use the motor effect (Fleming's left-hand rule) rather than being classified as electromagnet applications.
